facts.statement: Ardeadactylus is an extinct pterosaur named after the heron and finger, found in the Upper Jurassic Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria, southern Germany.
facts.quote: Ardeadactylus (from Ardea – meaning "heron", and also a name of a genus of herons – and dactylus, meaning "finger") is an extinct genus of ctenochasmatoid pterosaur known from the Upper Jurassic Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria, southern Germany.

facts.statement: Ardeadactylus is suspected to be a heron-like animal with a long neck and long legs that ate fish.
facts.quote: Ardeadactylus is suspected to be a heron–like, long–necked long–legged piscivore.

facts.statement: The neotype specimen of Ardeadactylus has an estimated wingspan of 1.45 meters, while another specimen is about 10% larger.
facts.quote: Bennett (2013) estimated the wingspan of the neotype specimen to be 1.45 m; the referred specimen from the Jura Museum is more or less 10% larger.

facts.statement: Ardeadactylus had fewer but larger teeth than Pterodactylus antiquus, suggesting it may have preyed on larger fish.
facts.quote: A. longicollum had fewer, fifteen per jaw, and relatively larger teeth than P. antiquus, possibly indicating that it preyed on larger fish than Pterodactylus.

facts.statement: Only two specimens of Ardeadactylus currently exist: one found in 1874 initially thought to be Pterodactylus suevicus, and a neotype held at the Jura Museum in Eichstätt.
facts.quote: Only two specimens of Ardeadactylus are known to exist currently: SMNS 56603 (earlier SMNS 5802) found in 1874, a specimen from Nusplingen initially thought to belong to the species Pterodactylus suevicus (currently Cycnorhamphus), and the neotype of the species, JME-SOS 2428, a specimen held at Jura Museum in Eichstätt.

facts.statement: The original holotype of Ardeadactylus was found near Eichstätt in 1853 and acquired by Professor Ludwig Frischmann for the Herzoglich Leuchtenbergische Naturalien-Kabinett.
facts.quote: The original holotype, consisting of the skull, neck and anterior torso, had been found near Eichstätt in 1853 and was that year acquired for the Herzoglich Leuchtenbergische Naturalien-Kabinett by Professor Ludwig Frischmann.

facts.statement: The destruction of the original holotype during World War II led Peter Wellnhofer to designate a neotype in 1970.
facts.quote: Its destruction motivated Peter Wellnhofer to assign a neotype in 1970.

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis placed Ardeadactylus in the family Aurorazhdarchidae as a sister taxon to Aurorazhdarcho.
facts.quote: In 2017, a phylogenetic analysis by Steven Vidovic and David Martill found Ardeadactylus within the family Aurorazhdarchidae, sister taxon to Aurorazhdarcho.

facts.statement: A 2018 analysis by Nicholas Longrich and colleagues recovered Ardeadactylus within the family Ctenochasmatidae instead of Aurorazhdarchidae.
facts.quote: In 2018 however, Nicholas Longrich and colleagues had recovered a different set of relationships for ctenochasmatoids. In their analysis, Ardeadactylus was recovered within the Ctenochasmatidae instead.

facts.statement: Ardeadactylus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 152.21 to 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Ardeadactylus was established by Bennett et al. in 2013.
The species Ardeadactylus longicollum was originally described by von Meyer in 1854.
